TINY BRUTALISM
A cozy little sandbox for making not-so-cozy architecture.

Tiny Brutalism is a relaxing freeform building game inspired by brutalist architecture.

Create strange monuments, impossible structures, concrete towers, or just a really big wall. 

There's no goal and no right way to build. Just make whatever you feel like making.

CONTROLS

* Click: build (click + hold to fill an area)

* Shift + click: remove

* Hold and scroll to flip through variants

* Ctrl/Cmd + Z: undo

* Click the sun icon to toggle day/night

* Esc: menu, settings and plot size

CAMERA

* Right-drag: orbit

* Middle-drag: pan

* Scroll: zoom

Please share your creations with me! Photos are saved locally. Use "Open Folder" in the settings to get them.

ReasoL3 days ago(+5)

hooo this is a good one ! i love those wooden block type games :D
Colors and texture are just right, and the selection of blocks is nice. 
tho one thing make the game meh in my opinion, and could use a bit more work : consistency. (LONG TEXT AHEAD)

Tiny-brutalism is hesitant between giving control or not to the player, and i believe the game would be better if you choose between the two option instead of the weird half/half that is going on now. Let me explain :

In townscaper, the player has no control over the decoration. the game has a fixed algorythm that make decoration appear whenever this or that shape is made. To build exaclty what the player want, he need to learn what patern of block make what decoration. 

In Tiny Glade, the player have a total control of what's going on. they decide were everything appear or not. The game wont create anything by itself.

Here in Tiny Brutalism, there is a weird in between were some features appearing by themself (mainly support and gutters) and other that the player have control over (doors, windows, plants). 
Also, some feature appears by themself AND i have control over, wich mean if i want a big empty wall, i make the wall then i need to remove every windows. I can't place a bridge but i need to remove those that appears, same with slopes that i can place but the game also randomly can.

I think Tiny brutalsim need a better disctinction between blocks, that the player place, and decoration, that happend by themselves. Either give me control of windows and dont place them randomly, or let the game decide were the windows end up. (the windows exemple is what's bothering me the most, but it is also true for slopes, bridges and cables.

Some Quality Of Life feature that would also be nice : 

Deleting and moving the view on the same input is not the greatest, a button to switch between "build" and "delete" would be nice. It could also make drag and delete possible.

Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+y - undo/redo are a must have

More keyboard shortcut in general ! don't keep that gem mouse only

the cycle between option is not the greatest at the moment. I know a menu with everything displayed is not the best option, but maybe copying the last placed block everytime, or something else ? 

Some content suggestion : 

Water, lilypads, and moss on the walls

full width stairs

Round collums, round windows, rounded slopes (like in a skatepark)

Blocks with real see through holes (square and circle ones 


I would gladly pay five or ten more dabloons for all of this ! you have a great game on hand, and i will love to see where its going !

Luc_Ienn3 days ago (6 edits) (+2)

Some feedback/requests: 

--The controls say "hold and scroll to flip through variants" but as far as I can tell this does not allow me to adjust or create pillars, or the diagonal supports. It would be nice to have some control over those features. Same with some randomly generated wall ridges that I would like to make on my own. I do understand that this makes it more like Tiny Glade (and Townscaper), though, so if that has to remain then I understand. I'm less bothered by the random drainpipes, that's fine. 

--Not sure if this is a bug, but if a bridge is generated at build height limit I cannot right-click the surface of a block at the edge of a structure to remove the bridge. I sort of wish there was a way to make bridges freeform, too. 

--Another thing that I noticed is that doors can only be built at ground level, so I cannot make a door on a balcony or on a raised platform up some stairs. Would be nice if doors were just part of the general wall decoration family for all surfaces.

--Lastly, it's a bit too easy to remove lights by accident! I cannot tell you how many times I'll be rotating the build, placing lights, and then realize I accidentally right clicked on a light while rotating and then deleted the light. Is it possible to just make the light-delete the usual shift-click instead?

This is such a fun little toy to play around in !!! As a self proclaimed eco-brutalist lover this scratches that itch very deeply for me. It's so easy to make something really gorgeous and although the fog is an eensy bit intense, it's still a really nice looking game. I really really appreciate the Mac build!!

I've put together some UI/UX suggestions that come out of some of the things I struggled with, but there's no obligation to use any of these (i'm a random stranger who just happens to have a design degree lol)

ThingIssueMy suggestion
Foliage iconsConfusing - the plant icon would indicate that you're placing down a plant, but it places down general shrubery/grass. Placing a tree requires you to click on an icon that looks like a pin, which is a bit oddleaf icon -> maybe something like grass?

pin icon -> tree icon
Changing variantsIt's not super clear how to switch between different variants, and the current system of was a bit frustrating as I often went past the one I wantedMaybe an interaction where you can hold down and a menu appears where you can select a particular variant? Alternatively, you could also copy what you did for light brightness and have a scroll wheel with some dots on the side to indicate different variants, so if you go past the one you want you can just scroll back
Time of dayJudging by the comments I'm not the only person who missed that you could change the time of day by clicking the sun icon. I thought that by dragging it downwards, it would make it nightI think it would be good to just split the current bar in half - top half is angle of the sun in the day and then past the middle point it becomes night, or something like that
Undo/redoNot in the UIUnfortunately people really need undo and redo buttons . i know the impulse to assume people will know command z. people do not know command z. just trust me on this one

Okay I bought the game and tried it out. I just want to say that looking forward to its development and like others have mentioned below, it has huge potential. Please, keep working at it.

Here is my 2 cents/review:

1. It definitely needs a way bigger lot. Why limit it to 8x8. Why not 64x64 for example? Or even bigger? Currently there's not more than a few minutes of gameplay.

2. Option/tool to decide what kind of block(s) each new block will be, instead of random generation. People really want to have that ability to build on their own terms

3. Options to reduce the fog / more weather options / overall better visibility

4. Lights to place. Lightpoles or any kind of lights

5. Some sort of backdrop option, besides only having plain gray

6. More settings/options. Ability to turn off the music, but keep some kind of ambient sound sound and block building sounds. The zoom/scroll needs option, because currently it is way too slow. I would prefer 5-10 x faster zooming

Overall, huge potential to build around this. I would hope to see this kind of game to be level based, where the player has tasks and limitations based on each level and that the gameplay deepens and widens as the player progresses through levels. It would be cool that the structures wouldn't build supporting pilars automatically, but it would be on the player's responsibility, so that the building doesn't collapse. This type of game could have really cool brutalism/megastructure lore too, but of course, that's totally up to you.

I would also recommend creating a Steam page to this with a demo-page where reviews are enabled, as it could get more traffic and feedback there. 

edit. I just noticed that there is lights. Didn't understand that when first trying it and that there is a star sky when in night mode
